sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in Philadelphia?
sections.html:
You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes it in its current condition. Each route ends at the same place: a deed recorded with the Philadelphia Department of Records and a transfer tax paid on it. The difference is how long you wait, how much work you do on the house first, and how much of the sale price reaches you after costs.

Philadelphia is unusual in Pennsylvania because the city and the county are one government. The city has been coterminous with Philadelphia County since 1854, so there is no separate county tax office to visit. The Office of Property Assessment, the Department of Revenue and the Department of Records are all city agencies, and that keeps the paperwork for a sale in one place.

  • Listing suits a house in good repair that can sit through showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • A sale by owner saves the agent's fee but leaves you handling the contract, the disclosure form and the settlement.
  • A cash offer fits a house with deferred repairs, a tangled title, a tenant, or an estate that needs to close out.

sections.h2: What does it cost to sell in Philadelphia?
sections.html:
The largest single cost that the city sets is the realty transfer tax. Since July 1, 2025 the combined rate has been 4.578%, made up of 3.578% for the city and 1% for the Commonwealth. The Department of Revenue says the rate had last moved in 2018, and the increase is earmarked for affordable housing programs.

On a $200,000 sale the combined rate comes to $9,156. The sales agreement decides which side pays it, so read that clause before you sign. The tax is due when the deed is recorded. The city allows up to 30 days to pay after the purchase, but the Department of Revenue suggests having it paid in full at closing, and you can pay online through the Philadelphia Tax Center.

When there is no sale price, such as a transfer between relatives, the tax is figured on the value that the Office of Property Assessment has set for the property.

sections.h2: Which transfers in Philadelphia are exempt from the transfer tax?
sections.html:
A transfer to a spouse, child or grandchild is exempt, and so is a transfer under a will. Every family exemption needs supporting documents filed with the deed, so gather them before the settlement date and do not assume the settlement agent will chase them for you.

The estate rule catches people out. A property passing under a will to several heirs is exempt on that transfer, but when those heirs then sell the house to a buyer, the sale is taxed. Anyone who inherited a Philadelphia house and plans to sell should budget for the full rate on the second step.

sections.h2: What is Philadelphia like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Philadelphia is the state's largest city, with an estimated 1,574,281 residents in July 2025, about 1.8% fewer than the April 2020 base. It covers 134.36 square miles of land and fits roughly 11,937 people into each of them, which is the density that makes rowhouse blocks the normal housing type. William Penn's charter dates to 1682, and the first row houses of the early 19th century earned the style the name Philadelphia rows.

Much of the housing stock dates to the 18th, 19th and early 20th centuries. Federal-style blocks stand in Old City and Society Hill, Victorian homes fill North Philadelphia, and twin houses are common in West Philadelphia. Wikipedia notes that this old stock has left vacant lots and decay in some areas, while Northern Liberties and Society Hill have been rehabilitated. A buyer or investor looking at an older rowhouse will price in the roof, the party walls and the plumbing, which is why condition drives offers more here than in newer suburbs.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $243,100, and 51.8% of homes are owner occupied (Census Bureau, 2020 to 2024).
  • Median gross rent: $1,397, with 679,428 households and 2.26 people per household.
  • Mean travel time to work: 31.7 minutes.
  • Summers are hot and humid, with about 30 days a year at or above 90 degrees, and winters average 22.4 inches of snow.

Large employers in the city include the University of Pennsylvania and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, and Temple University is the largest school by enrollment. Hospital and university jobs anchor demand in University City and the nearby rowhouse neighborhoods.

sections.h2: How do Philadelphia property taxes affect the sale?
sections.html:
The Office of Property Assessment sets values, and the Department of Revenue bills them. Bills for tax year 2027 go out on December 1, 2026, new assessments take effect January 1, 2027, and the payment is due March 31, 2027. For that year the First Level Review deadline was September 1, 2026 and the Board of Revision of Taxes deadline was October 5, 2026, so both windows have closed. Ask the Office of Property Assessment how to dispute a value for the following year.

The Homestead Exemption takes $100,000 off the taxable portion of an owner-occupied home's assessed value, and most owners save $1,399 a year. A mortgage or delinquent taxes do not block it, but a 10-year abatement does. An accepted application keeps working until the deed changes, so a buyer who will live in the house files their own application. The final date to apply is December 1 each year, and applying by October 1 puts the credit on the first bill.

  • An heir without their name on the deed can ask for a conditional Homestead Exemption, granted for up to three years, using a paper application marked Tangled Title.
  • Seniors and income-qualified owners can pay in eleven monthly installments if they apply by March 31.
  • The owner-occupied payment agreement can set a monthly payment as low as zero for past-due tax.

For a house with back taxes, ask the Department of Revenue for a payoff figure before you accept an offer, because delinquent tax is paid from the proceeds.

sections.h2: What disclosures and paperwork does Pennsylvania require from a Philadelphia seller?
sections.html:
A seller of residential property must give the buyer a signed property disclosure statement before the two sides sign the agreement of transfer. The Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law, 68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73, lists the topics: roof, basement, structure, plumbing, wiring, drainage, hazardous substances, title problems and more. You are not required to investigate, but you may not state anything you know is false or hide a known material defect.

Act 74, signed October 22, 2026, adds a flood insurance notice in section 7305.2. Sellers hand it to the buyer once the Insurance Department posts its flood information page. A buyer's damages claim under the law must be filed within two years after final settlement. Transfers by an executor or other fiduciary in settling an estate fall outside the chapter.

sections.h2: What should I do first if I need to sell a Philadelphia house quickly?
sections.html:
Start with the title and the tax bill, since those two items decide how fast a closing can happen. Pull the property record on the city's property search to see the assessed value, any homestead status and the amount owed, and then confirm whose names are on the deed.

  • Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and any mortgage payoff statement.
  • Collect proof of family relationship if the transfer might qualify for an exemption.
  • Decide whether the repairs you can afford will raise the price by more than they cost.
  • Compare a listing timeline against a cash offer's closing date, and ask each buyer to put the transfer tax split in writing.

A reputable buyer will explain the tax, the recording fee and the payoff line by line before you sign, and will let you walk away from the offer without charge.

faqs.q: How much is the Philadelphia transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: It is 4.578% of the price, or of the assessed value when there is no price. That is 3.578% for the city plus 1% for the Commonwealth, in effect since July 1, 2025. Your sales agreement decides who pays, and the tax is due when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Philadelphia house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes. Transfers under a will are exempt from transfer tax, but a later sale by the heirs is taxed. If your name is not on the deed, you may qualify for a conditional Homestead Exemption of up to three years while you sort out the title.

faqs.q: Does the Homestead Exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A buyer who will live in the home has to apply in their own name, because the exemption lasts only until the deed changes. The final date to apply is December 1 each year, and October 1 is the date to meet if the credit should appear on the first bill.

faqs.q: When are Philadelphia real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The tax is due March 31, and bills are mailed starting December 1 of the year before. Seniors and income-qualified owners can pay in eleven monthly installments if they apply by March 31. Ask the Department of Revenue for a payoff figure before closing.

faqs.q: What happens if a Philadelphia seller leaves out a known defect?
faqs.a: The seller can owe the buyer actual damages. Pennsylvania law lets a buyer sue a seller who willfully or negligently breaks the disclosure duties, and the suit must start within two years after final settlement. The sale itself is not undone by a missed disclosure.
